title: Testing the HTTP pipeline
summary: Run a minimal API in memory with TestServer, call it with HttpClient, and assert on status codes, headers and JSON: routing, binding, validation and DI lifetimes included. WebApplicationFactory explained.

steps.title: The whole pipeline, no network
body: A unit test of an endpoint's handler skips everything that breaks in real life: routing, model binding, validation, middleware, JSON settings, dependency injection. **Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost** runs the real app on an in-memory server; `HttpClient` calls go through the full pipeline without opening a port.

In a real solution you use **`WebApplicationFactory<Program>`** (package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing). It starts your actual `Program.cs` with a TestServer, lets you replace services, and is usually shared as a class fixture:
// Program.cs ends with: public partial class Program;   (so the test project can name it)
In this dojo the app and the tests live in one file, so the steps use TestServer directly: the app is built by a method that takes a `WebApplicationBuilder`, and the test adds `UseTestServer()`:
Same pipeline, same assertions; `WebApplicationFactory` does exactly this for you around `Program`.

steps.prompt: Which bugs does an in-memory pipeline test catch that a handler unit test misses?
buckets: A unit test catches it too
items: a service is registered as scoped and loses its data between requests
the JSON property is `TodoTitle` instead of `title`
the discount rule rounds the wrong way
a missing title returns 500 instead of 400
steps.explain: Anything about HTTP itself (routes, status codes, binding, serialization, DI wiring) needs the pipeline. Pure rules are cheaper to test without it.

steps.prompt: `POST /todos` returns 201, but a following `GET /todos/1` in the same test returns 404. The store is registered with `AddScoped<TodoStore>()`. Why?
options: A scoped service lives for one request: the GET gets a brand-new, empty store. Shared in-memory state must be a singleton
TestServer does not support GET after POST
steps.explain: Each HTTP request is a DI scope. This bug is invisible to unit tests, which construct the store by hand; only a test that sends two requests through the real container sees it.

steps.title: Integration tests for a todo API
prompt: The API, compiled beside your tests:
public record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Done);
public Todo Add(string title) { var t = new Todo(items.Count + 1, title, false); items.Add(t); return t; }
public Todo? Find(int id) => items.FirstOrDefault(t => t.Id == id);
app.MapGet("/todos/{id:int}", (int id, TodoStore store) => store.Find(id) is { } t ? Results.Ok(t) : Results.NotFound());
return Results.ValidationProblem(new Dictionary<string, string[]> { ["title"] = ["A title is required."] });

Write `public class TodoApiTests` with at least **4** async tests that start the app on a TestServer (add `using Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost;`) and call it over HTTP: create returns **201** with a `Location` header and the todo as JSON; the created todo can be read back; a blank title is **400**; an unknown id is **404**. Six planted bugs, including a DI lifetime.
starter: static async Task<(WebApplication App, HttpClient Client)> StartAsync()
solution: static async Task<(WebApplication App, HttpClient Client)> StartAsync()
var response = await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/todos", new { title = "  Write tests " }, Ct);
await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/todos", new { title = "Ship it" }, Ct);
var response = await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/todos", new { title }, Ct);

target: public record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Done);
public Todo Add(string title) { var t = new Todo(items.Count + 1, title, false); items.Add(t); return t; }
public Todo? Find(int id) => items.FirstOrDefault(t => t.Id == id);
app.MapGet("/todos/{id:int}", (int id, TodoStore store) => store.Find(id) is { } t ? Results.Ok(t) : Results.NotFound());
return Results.ValidationProblem(new Dictionary<string, string[]> { ["title"] = ["A title is required."] });

mutants.name: the Location header points to the wrong route
mutants.hint: Assert the Location header: other services follow it.

mutants.name: the store is scoped, so it forgets between requests
mutants.hint: Create a todo, then GET it in a second request.

hints: Start a fresh app in every test with the starter's helper, and dispose it: `var (app, client) = await StartAsync(); await using var _ = app;`.
`client.PostAsJsonAsync("/todos", new { title = "  Write tests " }, Ct)`, then check `StatusCode`, `Headers.Location` and `ReadFromJsonAsync<Todo>()`.
The DI bug only shows across two requests: POST, then `GetFromJsonAsync<Todo>("/todos/1")`.
steps.explain: Every test went through routing, binding, validation, DI and JSON, exactly as production traffic does, in a few milliseconds and with no port. The scoped-store bug is the classic one only such a test finds.
